## This release

Whole drives now finish. Earlier versions stopped every scan at 30 million
entries, so a large drive was read only part way. The limit now follows your
computer's memory: as many entries as fit in half of it, or in what the scan can
still allocate if that is less, and never under 30 million. That is up to about
35 million entries on 16 GB and 140 million on 64 GB. The CLI, the MCP server
and the app share it. Settings offers **Automatic** (the new default) plus larger
fixed limits. A saved 30 million limit from an earlier version reads as Automatic.

Measured on a real Windows system drive (55.4 million files, 5.9 million folders,
non-elevated): the scan finished in 269 s with a peak of 9.4 GB of memory, about
153 bytes per entry. The same drive previously stopped at 30 million entries.

**Clean up** is simpler. One switch picks **Safe to delete** (folders that tools
rebuild or re-download) or **Review first** (folders that may hold unique work),
and one **All kinds** menu narrows to one kind. A tick on each kind's heading
selects its safe folders. Counts, totals and **Select all safe** agree, and empty
folders are no longer listed. Removal rules and confirmation are unchanged, and
the MCP server stays read-only.
